Handler: This morning, greeting routines needs a look before the shift ends. We should keep the Companion Animal Travel Desk focused on calm intake and steady handoffs.
Planner: Use quiet voices near the kennels and confirm each carrier is secure before movement. The team should guide animals without sudden reaches or crowded spacing.
Coordinator: For Thornwick, <<FACT F028>> Review the lane for clean footing and keep water bowls ready for transit checks.
Handler: If Mia is on the manifest, watch for stress cues and pause for a slower pace. Gentle handling matters more than speed when an animal is uncertain.
Dispatcher: At the relief stop, <<FACT F016>> Send travelers there only after a brief escort and a clear reminder about leash control.
Planner: Report any loose latch, wet floor, or blocked path to the senior coordinator at once. Prevention is the first step in safe boarding work.
Coordinator: Share status only after the crate tags, documents, and traveler notes all match. Aurelia Skyways expects the same calm standard on every handoff.
Handler: Keep the tone steady with Noah Alvarez and Lucia Alvarez if they ask for an update. A clear, simple explanation helps reduce confusion at the desk.
Planner: Before closeout, walk the area again and confirm no feed, waste, or gear is left behind. Careful review keeps the Companion Animal Travel Desk ready for the next shift.
